newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand approves law against money laundering.
newsitem.headline: Thailand approves law against money laundering.

text.p: Thailand approved on Tuesday a new law against money laundering as part of a fight against drug trafficking and prostitution.

The law, approved by the cabinet and awaiting parliamentary ratification, was based on similar U.S. legislation that allows the government to monitor and intercept the transfer of finances by criminal suspects, Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said.
"This law permits official checks of suspicious financial flows in and out of the country," he told reporters
The new law calls for a money laundering suppresion agency, staffed by Finance Ministry and anti-narcotic officials.

Convictions under the new legislation would carry penalties ranging from one to 10-years in jail or a 200,000 baht ($7,692) fine, or a combination of both. It sets a maximum fine of one million baht ($38,500).
Thailand is viewed by Western anti-drug officials as a conduit for drugs from the opium-growing Golden Triangle of Thailand, Laos and Burma, and a centre for prostitution.

Legal expert Chaiyod Hemarachatha, who helped draft the law, told Reuters last month: "Thailand is a haven for criminals to launder dirty money, but I am confident when the new law comes into effect we can curb and deter their activities."
